Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said the development of Ladakh is a major priority
for the centre.
Mr Modi said this while addressing the people of Ladakh through video conferencing after
renaugurating five projects worth around Rs. 3,350 crore in the Union territory virtually.
In his address, the Prime Minister emphasized that the projects would improve connectivity,
strengthen electricity infrastructure, enhance water availability and boost the preservation
of Ladakh's ancient heritage.
The development and development of Ladakh is becoming more important.
In Ladakh today, many important development projects have been implemented.
With these efforts, many people's journey will be easy,
some of them will have better lighting facilities,
some of them will have better water supply,
and the protection of our ancient heritage will also be strengthened.
Mr Modi described the inauguration of these projects as another chapter in Ladakh's progress
and development. He said greater attention had been given to the development needs of
Ladakh after it became a union territory. He added that tourism opportunities in the
region are expanding, with winter and adventure tourism being promoted to generate employment.
The youth here got a good education and a chance to learn new technology.
And they didn't have to stay idle in other cities.
Because of this, a big centre of excellence is being formed.
IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu's Satellite Campus is also being advanced.
The Supreme Court has ruled that individuals converting from Hinduism to Islam or rather
non-Hindu religions cannot automatically claim reservation benefits under the backward class
category, dismissing the Tamil Nadu government's plea against a Madras High Court verdict.
A bench of justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sri Chandrasekhar held that social backwardness
suffered in an antecedent caste cannot be carried forward after conversion.
The apex court affirmed that conversion to a non-Hindu social order does not by itself
confer membership in any notified backward class community.
It declared that statutory benefits under Article 16-4 of the Constitution cannot be
extended solely on the basis of a person's pre-conversion status. The Court also reiterated
that anyone professing a religion other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism ceases to hold
scheduled caste status.
The Supreme Court has issued notice to Congress Leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party Chief
Akhilesh Yadav, and others on a plea challenging their march to the Court over alleged irregularities
in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of Electoral Roles. The court observed that nobody
can browbeat the judiciary. It also sought responses from the Chief Election Commissioner
Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a separate
petition filed by Gandhi and other opposition leaders alleging large-scale voter deletions
and irregularities in the SIR process.
A delegation of BJP women MPs today met Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and submitted a memorandum
regarding Congress MP Bimola Khojjam in connection with an alleged sexual harassment case at JNU.
Speaking to reporters BJP MP Dagubati Purandeshwari said, the internal committee of JNU had found
the Congress MP guilty.
She added that the delegation had urged the speaker to refer the matter to the Ethics
Committee and examine whether the Congress MP should still continue as a member of the
Lok Sabha.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the government is providing artificial limbs and other assistance
to tribal people in Chhattisgarh who have been left disabled by naturalism and supporting
them in leading a better life.
Mr. Shah said this while addressing the distribution ceremony of assistive devices
to persons with disabilities in Chhattisgarh through videoconferencing as part of the ongoing
Seva Sankal Pavyan. He said the government is making efforts to help those affected rebuild
their lives and ensure that they can live with dignity.
Narendra Modi government's firm resolve was that before 31st March, 2026, we will
end Nuxalism from the entire country and I am happy that Nuxalism has been ended.
But by the end of Nuxalism, we cannot end the pain of these five decades.
We will have to put an end to the pain that has been inflicted on the villages.
We will have to try to rebuild them.
And we will have to make arrangements so that they can live with respect.
We will have to give them the strength to stand on their feet again.
We will have to make arrangements for this.
And many positive results have come out of this.
In Punjab, a Panth call has been given in protest against the broad daylight murder
of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa on Tuesday and the prevailing drug
menace in the state. It is experiencing a mixed response. Markets in several parts of
the state are closed, main and interior roads in some parts have been blocked. Release have
made arrangements for maintaining peace a report.
Several political parties, farmer unions and traders' organizations have extended
sport to the band call which was materialized on the appeal of Bhim Singh, father of the
slain anti-drug crusader. He urged people yesterday to come out and ensure the band's success.
The protesters are however allowing ambulances and other emergency vehicles to pass. The
action committee formed to seek justice in the case has appealed to people to maintain
peace and remain calm during the band. There is no information of any unturbert
incidents from anywhere in the state as of now. The band has been called from 6 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Meanwhile, family of Parvinder Singh has not allowed the authorities to conduct his post-mortem,
as they are demanding to form a panel of doctors from PGI Chandigarh to do the process.
Rajesh Bali, Akashwani News, Jalandhar
President Ropade Murmur has called for greater economic empowerment of rural women,
asserting that their active participation in nation building
will be crucial to achieving the vision of Iqasid Bharat before 2047.
The President inaugurated the National Sarasmela 2026 in Vijaywada today in the presence of
Andhra Pradesh Gavna S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and several
Union and State Ministers.
Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Murmur said that women associated with self-help groups
were becoming self-reliant and contributing significantly to their families, the rural
economy and national development.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the government has been ceaselessly working towards
achieving the goal of a vikasidh Bharat by 2047. Today in our special series, we bring
you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through Veti Bachao,
Veti Parhao, a flagship campaign of the government of India.
Veti Bachao, Veti Parhao, a flagship campaign was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi
on January 22, 2015 from Panipat in Haryana.
The campaign has played a pivotal role in empowering the daughters and proving the sex
ratio in Haryana.

Mr. Jagaland, the former Sarpancho Bibipur village and gene district and the initiator of the selfie with daughter campaign stated that the Beti Bachao Beti Padau initiative has led to increased participation of daughters across all sectors in Haryana.
In the past, there were very few girls in Haryana, who had very low blood sugar levels.
Haryana girls had very low blood sugar levels, but if we look at it today,
Haryana girls have around 75% blood sugar levels, which was around 64% before 2014.
Along with that, if we talk about the co-position of the girls, they have very low blood sugar levels.
It is noteworthy, motivated by the PM's spirit of Jan Seva Siddish Seva,
Sunil Jagalan, Selfie with daughter campaign, contributed a lot in feeling the people
proud after posting Selfie with their daughters.
Prime Minister Menendar Modi frequently mentioned Sunil Jagalan's Selfie with daughter campaign
in his monkey bath program and helped transform it into a nationwide movement.
Originating from a remote area, this initiative has now evolved into a global campaign.
Ashwani Kumar Sharma, Akashwani News, Chandigarh.

Defense Minister Rajnath Singh has said that India is exporting indigenous defense products
to nearly 100 countries worldwide. He said that India's defense exports have surged from
just 686 crore rupees in 2013-14 to more than 38,000 crore rupees in 2025-26, speaking at
the Defense Conclave 2026 of a private channel in New Delhi today. Mr Singh said India has
achieved more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants.
Hope for the peace, but prepare for war.
War that may be necessary to protect our country's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sita Raman met the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healy
on the sidelines of the annual meetings in Bangkok today during the meeting
the Finance Minister reaffirmed India's commitment to working closely with the UK towards shared
priorities and a constructive, inclusive G20 process.
Nirmala Sitaraman arrived in Bangkok today to attend the annual meetings of the International
Monetary Fund and the World Bank. She will also participate in the G20 and G7 Finance
Ministers and Central Bank governors' meetings.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with the Indian contingent that participated
in the Asian Games 2026 in New Delhi this evening.
The Prime Minister will also address the gathering on the occasion.
Intern wrestler Vishwajit Ramchandra More has created history
by clinching a historic silver medal in the Greco-Roman finals
at the Under-23 World Championships in Las Vegas today.
Competing in the men's 55kg category, More narrowly lost
past 12.13 to George S. Gopakarumidze in the final seconds of the bout.
The Intervitological Department has focused heavy to very heavy rainfall, expected over

over Kerala, Mahittamul Nadu, Bouddhicherry and Karyakal till the 21st of this month.
The higher reaches of Dota District in Jammu and Kashmir experienced the season's first
snowfall. And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
